title.narrative: IPU Inter-Parliamentary Union 2022-2024 (2026) - IPU Inter-Parliamentary Union 2022-2024 (2026) - ISK

description.narrative:
IPU är en global organisation av parlament som bildades 1889 i syfte att arbeta för fred och mellanfolkligt samarbete. IPU består idag av 178 nationella parlamentsmedlemmar och 13 associerade medlemmar som utgörs av regionala parlament. IPU arbetar i nära samverkan med FN samt med internationella och lokala organisationer. IPU har sedan 2002 observatörsstatus i FN:s generalförsamling. Sekretariatet ligger i Genève och de har ett FN-kontor i New York. IPU’s sekretariat har idag 40 anställda.
IPU:s verksamhet syftar till att främja och stärka parlamentens lagstiftande, granskande och representativa funktioner. De har ett särskilt fokus på mänskliga rättigheter, jämställdhet, ungas deltagande och inflytande, fred och konfliktförebyggande samt parlamentens ansvar och roll i att stödja arbetet för de Globala målen för hållbar utveckling. Detta genom att skapa förutsättningar för och uppmuntra dialog mellan parlament och parlamentsledamöter världen över, genom att bedriva forskning och utveckla standarder och riktlinjer för god demokratisk parlamentarisk praxis och genom riktade kapacitetsutvecklande insatser till enskilda parlament i utvecklingsländer.

Inter-parliamentary Union (IPU) is the world organisation of national parliaments with 178 members. IPU's vision is a world where every voice counts, where democracy and parliaments are at the service of the people for peace and development. With a broad membership base IPU has the potential to reach a big majority of the world's lawmakers, and this is done through political initiatives by members and through program work initiated by the secretariat. Its political dimension enables parliaments and their members to voice their views and concerns and adopt common strategies and commitments at the international level. The political nature of the organization serves as a powerful conduit to catalyse change at national level. Discussions and debates held within the organization, often on sensitive issues, open space for dialogue and push members of parliament (MP) to engage on issues potentially sensitive in a national context. Such dialogues and debates expose MPs to diverse points of views and experiences. Added to peer-to-peer learning and influence, IPU Assemblies and political gatherings serve as platforms that encourage MPs from around the world to regularly assess their work and the work of their parliament. The resolutions adopted by the organization on those occasions serve as a framework for action and can facilitate action by parliaments at the national level. Through its programme work, IPU develops support to parliaments, focussing first on building their capacity to effectively carry out their constitutional mandate to pass laws, exercise governmental oversight, adopt budgets and represent the public.
The support is a programme support to four of IPU's five strategic objectives with a particular focus on SO1 (Effective and empowered parliaments).

The IPU's strategy 2022-2026 focuses on five strategic priorities (objectives) aimed at building effective parliamentary ecosystems and identifies seven policy goals that are a priority for parliaments and require urgent action.
SO1: Building effective and empowered parliaments SO2: Promoting inclusive and representative parliaments SO3: Supporting resilient and innovative parliaments SO4: Catalysing collective parliamentary action SO5: Strengthening the IPUs accountability (not funded by Sida)
The policy goals are to be reached through the strategic objectives. The seven policy goals have a number of formulated targets that IPU aim to strive for during the intervention. The policy goals are the following.
PG 1: Climate change PG 2: Democracy and strong parliaments PG 3: Human rights PG 4: Gender equality PG 5: Youth participation PG 6: Peace and security PG 7: Sustainable Development Goals
